hero.title: Hekla, on the horizon.
hero.intro: A quiet view toward one of Iceland’s most storied volcanoes—shared from Úlfagreni, with room for a future live camera when the mountain has something to say.

history.heading: Hekla’s recorded story
history.intro: Hekla is a ridge-shaped volcano with a fissure along its summit. Its eruptions have varied enormously—some began explosively, others produced long lava flows. Written records reach back to 1104, while layers in Icelandic soil preserve a much older story.

eras.title: Layers in the earth
eras.description: Large prehistoric eruptions left the Hekla-5, Hekla-4 and Hekla-3 tephra layers—time markers found far beyond the mountain.

eras.title: Accounts and ash
eras.description: The first recorded eruption in 1104 began a long written chronology of explosive openings, lava flows and difficult years for nearby farms.

eras.title: The monitored volcano
eras.description: Six modern eruption episodes transformed what scientists know about Hekla and how quickly its warning signs may appear.

field_notes.title: Not one simple cone
field_notes.description: Hekla combines features of a central volcano and an eruptive fissure. The summit fissure is called Heklugjá.

field_notes.title: A remarkable record
field_notes.description: The Icelandic Meteorological Office describes Hekla as Iceland’s third most active volcanic system in historical time.

field_notes.title: Watch the experts
field_notes.description: Activity is assessed by scientists using seismic, deformation, and other data. Conditions can change quickly; official notices matter.

official_heading: Use official sources for activity and travel decisions.
footer_text: A personal project about the view toward Hekla from Úlfagreni.
